+## 2026-10-05 -- Package 2, Stage 2, batch 4: item 7b (P2-1), Beltrami scaling, and Beltrami's GPU path repaired
+
+**Series** (Section 10): the pinned configuration of Section 6.7 at N_vel = 6, 7, 8 with N_p = 8, 9, 10,
+i.e. P = 7,984, 13,764 and 22,288, on interior grids 8^4, 10^4 and 11^4. Same protocol as
+Kovasznay (batch 3): its own process, warm-up, one timed run with the diagnostics off, peak
+memory, then errors and kappa/rank off the clock.
+
+**Errors** are the paper's: u, v, w, p and the pin-gauge p at each snapshot time (t = 1
+included), and the time-averaged relative L2 errors (`rel_l2_*`).
+
+**The rule for the larger sizes.** Section 10 fixes the interior grids and asks for "the boundary
+rows and the eight pressure pins generated by the same rule as the paper's run for the respective
+grid". The code's collocation table has no clean rule across N_vel (N_bc = 5, 6, 6 for N_vel = 4,
+5, 6). The paper's own run gives N_ic = the grid (8) and N_bc = N_t_bc = the grid - 2 (6), and
+that relation is applied:
+
+| N_vel | grid | N_bc = N_t_bc | N_ic |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 7 | 10 | 8 | 10 |
+| 8 | 11 | 9 | 11 |
+
+The pins are one per temporal level, i.e. N_p of them: 8 at the paper size, 9 and 10 above. The
+pressure's spatially constant temporal modes T_j(t) x 1, j < N_p, enter only the pin rows: one pin
+leaves an (N_p - 1)-dimensional null space (Package 1, Section 3.7), and N_p pins close it. So 8
+pins at N_p = 9 would leave the system rank-deficient. "Eight" is read as the paper's count, not
+a fixed number. **To state in the report.**
+
+`beltrami_config(6)` equals `run_beltrami_pinned.pinned_config()` exactly (tested). The rows are
+`beltrami_rows`: 4 equations per interior point, 3 velocity components on the 6 faces and at
+t = 0, and the pins. That count is checked against an assembled system, and gives the paper's
+21,816 rows at N_vel = 6.
+
+**Beltrami's GPU path was broken, and is repaired.** `problems.beltrami._lstsq` called
+`torch.linalg.lstsq(driver='gelsd')`. PyTorch refuses that on CUDA ("driver other than gels is not
+supported on CUDA"), so no Beltrami GPU solve could ever complete. Package 1 ran Beltrami only on
+the CPU, so it was never exercised. The branch also fell back to the CPU silently when no GPU was
+present.
+- **Fix:** the GPU branch now uses Kovasznay's validated GPU solver
+  (`problems.kovasznay._lstsq_gpu_qr`: Householder QR, Q^T b from the reflectors, triangular
+  solve; the algorithm of LAPACK's `gels`; full rank assumed), with its timing parts and peak
+  memory. Section 10's "both devices run identical systems" holds by construction.
+- Without a GPU, the branch now raises.
+- **The CPU path is unchanged:** the paper's pinned Beltrami run (CPU, diagnostics off) gives
+  coefficients and coefficient changes identical bit for bit to ab0484d.
+- On the laptop GPU a small Beltrami system agrees with the CPU to 1e-8 (tested).
+
+**Shared code, passive.** `solve_beltrami` keeps per-iteration `t_assemble`, `t_solve`,
+`gpu_mem_peak_bytes` and `gpu_parts`, and returns the final system on request
+(`return_final_system`), as Kovasznay's does.
+
+**C8' for Beltrami.** The paper point is the pinned run (`beltrami_pinned`, clean CPU time 267 s).
+Every snapshot error and the pin-gauge time-averaged pressure error must match to 1e-10, and the
+CPU time must be within 15%. There is no paper Beltrami GPU point, so C8' has a GPU part only for
+Kovasznay. **Attainable on Grace:** package1's pinned run and its K_max pass (separate jobs), and
+the unpinned paper run (wave 2) against its K_max pass (wave 1), agree bit for bit on `norm_R_h`.
+
+**A size that does not fit in 40 GB** is recorded as `did_not_fit`: the error, P, N and the bytes
+of A (Section 10). Any other failure still stops the job.
+
+**Jobs:**
+- `p2s2_scaling_cpu_a` adds Beltrami N_vel = 6, 7.
+- `p2s2_scaling_cpu_b` (new; timed-cpu, 5.5 h) is N_vel = 8 alone, about 1.6 h per run scaled
+  as P^3 from 267 s. 5.5 h x 48 SU/h = 264 SU is under Section 1's 300-SU skip threshold, so it
+  runs.
+- `p2s2_scaling_gpu` adds all three Beltrami sizes.
+- Each job writes its provenance to its own folder (`provenance_<device>_<job id>`), since the
+  two CPU jobs may run at the same time.
+
+REHEARSAL_PLACEHOLDER
+
+Tests: `tests/test_p2s2_scaling.py`.
